rationale: Distinct from the proper-noun usage (epithet of Zarathustra). Here functions as qualitative adjective modifying an implied time-noun: 'the chosen [moment] in which the Andrias goes up.' Doubled -ⲧⲧ supports qualitative reading.

Lyc ⲁⲟⲩⲏⲧ = Sah. ⲟⲩⲏⲧ 'single, joined, sole' (cf. accumulated ⲛ̄ϣⲃⲣ̄ⲁⲟⲩⲏⲧ 'yokefellow'). With article = 'the unity, the single body.' Here 'the unity of this great Andrias' = the integral wholeness of the Last Statue from which the lost souls are cut off.
Glossary has ⲗⲁⲓⲟ̄ⲉ tentatively as 'occasion/matter.' With particle ⲣⲱ ('indeed, then'), strengthens to 'the very cause, the cause indeed.' Confirms the 'cause' reading over 'occasion.'
Future ⲛⲁ- + ⲧⲉϩ- (Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱϩ 'reach, attain') + 3pl object suffix -ⲁⲩ. Construction ⲙⲛ̄ X ⲛⲁⲧⲉϩⲁⲩ = 'no X shall reach them.' Eschatological terminus formula.
Lyc ⲡⲏⲱ qualitative likely from ⲡⲏϣ̄ 'be afflicted, grieved' (cf. Sah ⲡⲱϣ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ). Compound idiom: 'grieved-of-heart.' Recurs lines 18, 20 of this page in the firmaments' lamentation.
Recurring verb ll.3, 11, 21. Lyc reflex of ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'cut, sever' or related root. Eschatological-soteriological severance from the Andrias. Confirmed by directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄- 'from.'

Ordinal ⲙⲁϩ-ϩⲧⲁⲩ 'fourth' (Lyc) + ⲣⲓⲙⲉ 'weeping.' The Manichaean 'fourth weeping' is the firmaments' lament — distinct from three prior cosmic weepings (perhaps of apostles, Fathers, prophets enumerated on previous pages).

Hapax in this corpus. Context (firmaments grieving over souls) requires a noun of mourning/grief-utterance. Possibly Lyc form of ⲁϣⲁϩⲟⲙ 'sigh' or related lament-stem. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.
ⲕⲉ- ('other') + ⲱⲁⲙⲧ (= Lyc ϣⲟⲙⲧ̄ 'three') + ⲛ̄ⲣⲓⲙⲉ + ⲛ̄ⲱⲁⲣⲡⲧ ('first/foremost'). Confirms a cosmic schema of multiple weepings, the four together forming an enumerated set.

Standard Manichaean eschatological term — already in accumulated vocabulary as ⲡⲙⲟⲩ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ. This page uses the ordinal form ⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'second' attributively. Same referent: the eternal binding of unredeemed souls in the bōlos.

Relative ⲉⲧ- + ⲟⲩⲁϩⲉ 'stand, be present' — 'that stands (over them).' Idiomatic for difficulties/necessities that confront one. The apostles met every toil and every necessity that arose against them.
